headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks between dexter and kestra.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and kestra reads/writes files plus runs declarative workflows, so a shared workspace could let dexter-produced content be treated as instructions by kestra. No direct shared-channel proof exists, but both profiles expose file-based I/O and autonomous execution, so the interaction is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or mounted volume
IF kestra ingests dexter-generated files as workflow inputs without sanitization
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct directories
Disable automatic workflow ingestion from shared files
Add a manual review step for any dexter-generated artifact before kestra consumes it
Use read-only mounts for dexter outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between producer and consumer

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter handles financial and market data and has broad network egress to multiple APIs; kestra can read files, logs, database data, cloud storage data, and send data to many external services. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive data can flow from dexter into kestra and then outward through kestra's integrations.
conditions: IF dexter outputs financial data into a location kestra can read
IF kestra forwards those files, logs, or variables to Slack, email, cloud, or HTTP destinations
mitigations: Keep dexter and kestra on separate workspaces
Restrict kestra connectors to approved destinations only
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Rotate any shared API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention rules on kestra outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both can write or mutate shared resources: dexter has autonomous execution with file output, while kestra can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, write the filesystem, and use elevated privileges. Without locking or isolation, concurrent writes and side effects can collide and corrupt state.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem, database, or cloud resource
IF kestra workflows and dexter tasks run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories
Serialize access to shared resources
Disable root and docker.sock unless required
Use per-agent service accounts
requires-engineering: add distributed locks around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter can generate research outputs from APIs, and kestra can turn inputs into automated workflows, notifications, emails, or infrastructure actions. If kestra treats dexter output as authoritative, a bad or manipulated research result can cascade into irreversible downstream actions.
conditions: IF kestra uses dexter output as a workflow parameter or trigger
IF no validation step checks dexter facts before notifications or actions
mitigations: Require human approval before actioning dexter output
Validate dexter outputs against independent sources
Limit kestra to dry-run mode for dexter-fed workflows
Log and review all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add schema and provenance checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: dexter touches financial data and market data, while kestra handles logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if the same regulated data is routed through kestra's broader operational surfaces; no single-agent compliance block is documented, so the risk is moderate rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is routed into kestra logs, notifications, or cloud connectors
IF retention or residency settings differ between dexter and kestra
mitigations: Exclude regulated fields from kestra logs
Set short retention on kestra artifacts
Review destination regions for cloud connectors
Document the data-handling boundary
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data
